obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must ensure inactive, non-operational UCCs are not misused.
obligations.action_required: Implement a mechanism to prevent misuse of inactive, non-operational UCCs.
obligations.evidence_type: Mechanism documentation and audit trails

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must ensure inactive, non-operational UCCs are weeded out during client UCC mapping.
obligations.action_required: Implement a mechanism to weed out inactive, non-operational UCCs during the process of mapping clients’ UCC with their demat account.
obligations.evidence_type: Mapping process documentation and audit trails

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must provide a copy of the SEBI-devised uniform documentation to clients.
obligations.action_required: Provide a copy of the SEBI-devised uniform documentation to clients.
obligations.evidence_type: Client acknowledgement of receipt of documentation; documentation provided to client

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must use the KYC template finalised by CERSAI and specified by SEBI as Part I of AOF for individuals and legal entities.
obligations.action_required: Use the KYC template finalised by CERSAI and specified by SEBI through various circulars as Part I of AOF for individuals and legal entities.
obligations.evidence_type: Completed KYC form as per CERSAI and SEBI specifications

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must onboard new clients by April 01, 2024.
obligations.action_required: Complete the onboarding of new clients by April 01, 2024.
obligations.evidence_type: Client onboarding completion records; system logs of compliance

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must inform existing clients about MITC via email or suitable mode by June 01, 2024.
obligations.action_required: Inform existing clients about MITC via email or any other suitable mode of communication.
obligations.evidence_type: Email records or other communication records

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers that are also depository participants must use the KYC form for basic details and collect additional information for demat accounts.
obligations.action_required: Use the KYC form (as specified at para 21.1.2.1) for basic client details and collect additional information for demat accounts.
obligations.evidence_type: Completed KYC form with additional demat account information

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must provide standard documents to clients as part of the account opening kit, in the client's preferred format (electronic or physical).
obligations.action_required: Make available standard documents to clients as part of the account opening kit, in the client's preferred format (electronic or physical).
obligations.evidence_type: Completed account opening form; electronic document logs (if documents are made available electronically)

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must seek client preference for document format (electronic or physical) as part of the account opening form.
obligations.action_required: Seek client preference for document format (electronic or physical) as part of the account opening form.
obligations.evidence_type: Completed account opening form

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must maintain logs if documents are made available in electronic form.
obligations.action_required: Maintain logs of electronic documents made available to clients.
obligations.evidence_type: Electronic document logs

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must not introduce voluntary clauses/docs that stand in conflict with mandatory documents/rules.
obligations.action_required: Ensure that any voluntary clause/document introduced in the existing as well as new documents does not stand in conflict with any of the clauses in the mandatory documents, Rules, Bye-laws, Regulations, Notices, Guidelines and Circulars issued by SEBI and the Stock Exchanges.
obligations.evidence_type: Documentation review records; compliance audit reports

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must obtain client signature on the Account Opening Form.
obligations.action_required: Obtain client signature on the Account Opening Form.
obligations.evidence_type: Signed Account Opening Form

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must obtain client acknowledgement of Most Important Terms and Conditions (MITC).
obligations.action_required: Obtain client acknowledgement of Most Important Terms and Conditions (MITC).
obligations.evidence_type: Acknowledgement of MITC

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must obtain specific authorization from clients for Running Account facility, Power of Attorney, Demat Debit and Pledge Instruction, etc.
obligations.action_required: Obtain specific authorization from clients for Running Account facility, Power of Attorney, Demat Debit and Pledge Instruction, etc.
obligations.evidence_type: Specific authorization documents

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must register new clients on all active stock exchanges after obtaining trading preferences.
obligations.action_required: Register new clients on all active stock exchanges after obtaining trading preferences in the aforementioned format.
obligations.evidence_type: Client registration records on stock exchanges; email/SMS records of client notification

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must offer existing clients access to all active stock exchanges for opted segments within 3 months.
obligations.action_required: Offer existing clients access to all active stock exchanges for opted segments as a default mode within 3 months from the effective date of the circular.
obligations.deadline_rule: within 3 months from the effective date of the circular
obligations.evidence_type: Client access records on stock exchanges; email/SMS records of client notification

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must inform clients of access offer via email/SMS.
obligations.action_required: Inform clients of access offer via email/SMS.
obligations.evidence_type: Email/SMS records of client notification

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must allow clients to opt out of access.
obligations.action_required: Allow clients to opt out of access by providing negative consent.
obligations.evidence_type: Client opt-out records

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must activate/deactivate segments based on client preferences.
obligations.action_required: Activate/deactivate segments based on client preferences.
obligations.evidence_type: Segment activation/deactivation records

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers registered exclusively with commodity derivatives exchanges must use the FMC-prescribed format for Trading Preferences.
obligations.action_required: Use the format for Trading Preferences as prescribed by the erstwhile Forward Markets Commission (FMC) vide its circular no. FMC/COMPL/IV/KRA-05/11/14 dated February 26, 2015.
obligations.evidence_type: Completed Trading Preferences documentation set as prescribed by FMC

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must provide an opting out facility to new and existing clients.
obligations.action_required: Provide opting out facility to new and existing clients.
obligations.evidence_type: Client opting out request records

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must obtain written negative consent from clients for opting out.
obligations.action_required: Obtain written negative consent from clients for opting out.
obligations.evidence_type: Client negative consent records

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must maintain client negative consent records for at least 5 years.
obligations.action_required: Maintain records of written negative consent provided by clients for at least five years.
obligations.evidence_type: Client negative consent records

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must conduct securities market activities in GIFT-IFSC under a Separate Business Unit (SBU) of the stock broking entity.
obligations.action_required: Conduct securities market activities in GIFT-IFSC under a Separate Business Unit (SBU) of the stock broking entity.
obligations.evidence_type: SBU designation records; branch qualification documentation

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must designate a branch as a Separate Business Unit (SBU) to conduct securities market activities in GIFT-IFSC.
obligations.action_required: Designate a branch as a Separate Business Unit (SBU) to conduct securities market activities in GIFT-IFSC.
obligations.evidence_type: SBU designation records; branch qualification documentation

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must segregate and ring-fence securities market activities of their SBU in GIFT-IFSC from Indian securities market activities.
obligations.action_required: Segregate and ring-fence securities market activities of the SBU in GIFT-IFSC from Indian securities market activities. Maintain an arms-length relationship between these activities.
obligations.evidence_type: Documentation of segregation and ring-fencing procedures; records of arms-length relationship maintenance

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must exclusively engage in securities market related activities in GIFT-IFSC as permitted by IFSCA.
obligations.action_required: Operate the SBU in GIFT-IFSC exclusively for securities market related activities as permitted by IFSCA.
obligations.evidence_type: Business plan and operational documentation for SBU in GIFT-IFSC

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must ensure SBU activities in GIFT-IFSC are as permitted by IFSCA.
obligations.action_required: Ensure that the activities carried out by the SBU in GIFT-IFSC are as permitted by IFSCA.
obligations.evidence_type: Documentation of SBU activities in GIFT-IFSC, IFSCA approvals

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers who have floated a subsidiary or entered into a joint venture for securities market activities in GIFT-IFSC may dismantle it and carry out services under an SBU of the stock broking entity.
obligations.action_required: Dismantle a subsidiary/joint venture undertaking securities market activities in GIFT-IFSC and carry out services under an SBU of the stock broking entity.
obligations.evidence_type: Board resolution or minutes to dismantle subsidiary/joint venture and records of SBU setup

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must segregate and ring-fence NDS-OM activities from securities market activities.
obligations.action_required: Segregate and ring-fence NDS-OM activities from securities market activities of the stock broker.
obligations.evidence_type: Documentation of segregation and ring-fencing measures, including organizational structure and controls

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must maintain an arms-length relationship between NDS-OM and securities market activities.
obligations.action_required: Maintain an arms-length relationship between NDS-OM activities and securities market activities of the stock broker.
obligations.evidence_type: Documentation of organizational structure and controls to maintain arms-length relationship

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must exclusively engage in NDS-OM transactions within their SBU.
obligations.action_required: Ensure the SBU is exclusively engaged in NDS-OM transactions.
obligations.evidence_type: SBU activity logs, transaction records

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must prepare and maintain a separate account for the SBU on an arms-length basis.
obligations.action_required: Prepare and maintain a separate account for the SBU on an arms-length basis.
obligations.evidence_type: Separate account records for SBU, audited financial statements

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must keep the net worth of their SBU segregated from their own net worth in the securities market.
obligations.action_required: Segregate the net worth of the SBU from the net worth of the stock broker in the securities market.
obligations.evidence_type: Financial records showing segregation of SBU net worth from stock broker net worth

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must satisfy their net worth criteria after excluding the account of the SBU.
obligations.action_required: Exclude the account of the SBU when calculating the net worth criteria for the stock broker.
obligations.evidence_type: Financial records showing exclusion of SBU account from net worth calculation

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must inform investors that Grievance Redressal Mechanism and Investor Protection Fund (IPF) of the stock exchanges and SCORES are not available for investors availing the services of the SBU.
obligations.action_required: Inform investors that Grievance Redressal Mechanism and Investor Protection Fund (IPF) of the stock exchanges and SCORES are not available for investors availing the services of the SBU.
obligations.evidence_type: Notification or disclosure to investors regarding unavailability of Grievance Redressal Mechanism and Investor Protection Fund (IPF) of the stock exchanges and SCORES

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock exchanges must prescribe financial disincentives on stock brokers for serious lacunas found in the system audit process and/or non-closure of observations within defined timelines.
obligations.action_required: Prescribe financial disincentive on SBs for instances where serious lacunas found in the system audit process and/or non-closure of observations found during the audit within defined timelines.
obligations.evidence_type: Financial disincentive policy and records of enforcement

obligations.obligation_summary: Stock brokers must ensure voluntary clauses/docs do not dilute their responsibility or conflict with mandatory documents/rules.
obligations.action_required: Review and ensure that any voluntary clause/document added does not dilute the responsibility of the stock broker and is not in conflict with any of the clauses in the mandatory documents, Rules, Bye-laws, Regulations, Notices, Guidelines and Circulars issued by SEBI and the Stock Exchanges.
obligations.evidence_type: Documentation review records; compliance audit reports

reporting_ground_truth.description: The member shall carry out complete internal audit on a half yearly basis and shall forward the report along with para-wise comments to the respective Stock Exchange/ Clearing Corporation within two months from the end of the half year period.
The stock brokers shall inform the Stock Exchanges of existing and new bank account(s) in the format specified at Table 2.
The stock brokers shall inform the Stock Exchanges of existing and new demat account(s) in the format specified at Table 3.
Stock Brokers shall ensure that the internal audit reports are submitted to the Exchanges within two months of the end of respective half years for which the audit is being conducted.

Stock Brokers shall submit financial statements to Stock Exchanges in the same format as prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013 irrespective of whether they fall under the purview of the Companies Act, 2013 or not. The due date for submission of the aforesaid financial statements to Stock Exchanges shall be the same as prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013 for submission to Registrar of Companies.
The Stock Brokers shall upload the data (specified at para 15.9.1) on a monthly basis for every client onto each Stock Exchange system where the broker is a member

The brokers shall be required to furnish the particulars (mentioned at para 20.1 and 20.2.1) of their clients to the Stock Exchanges/Clearing Corporations and the same would be updated on a monthly basis. Such information for a specific month should reach the exchange within seven working days of the following month.
Stock Brokers shall upload the details of clients, such as, name, mobile number, address for correspondence and E- mail address to Stock Exchanges

The stock brokers shall submit to the Stock Exchange a half-yearly certificate, as on 31st March and 30th September of each year, from an auditor confirming the net 232 worth. Such a certificate shall be submitted not later than 30th April and 31st October of every year.

The stock broker shall disclose to the Stock Exchanges details on gross exposure towards margin trading facility including name of the client, Category of holding (Promoter/promoter group or Non-promoter), clients' PAN, name of the scrips (Collateral stocks and Funded stocks) and if the stock broker has borrowed funds for the purpose of providing margin trading facility, name of the lender and amount borrowed, on or before 12 noon on the following trading day. The format for this disclosure by the stock broker to the stock exchange is enclosed at Annexure-15.

The books of accounts, maintained by the broker, with respect to the margin trading facility offered by it, shall be audited on a half yearly basis. The stock broker shall submit an auditor’s certificate to the exchange within one month from the date of the half year ending 31st March and 30th September of a year certifying, inter alia, the extent of compliance with the conditions of margin trading facility.

On a daily basis,  TM shall report disaggregated information on collaterals up to the level of its clients to the CM.  CM shall report disaggregated information on collaterals up to the level of clients of TM and proprietary collaterals of the TMs to the Stock Exchanges (SEs) and CCs in respect of each segment.

& 59.6 The stock brokers / trading members that provide the facility of algorithmic trading shall subject their algorithmic trading system to a system audit every six months in order to ensure that the requirements prescribed by SEBI / stock exchanges with regard to algorithmic trading are effectively implemented. Deficiencies or issues identified during the process of system audit of trading algorithm / software shall be reported by the stock broker / trading member to the stock exchange immediately on completion of the system audit.

All registered Stock Brokers using AI / ML based application or system as defined in Annexure 27, are required to fill in the form (Annexure 26) and make submissions on quarterly basis within fifteen calendar days of the expiry of the quarter. 233

Stock Brokers shall disclose on their respective websites, the data on complaints received against them or against issues dealt by them and redressal thereof, latest by seventh of succeeding month, as per the format enclosed at Annexure-38.

The URL to the website of a stock broker shall be reported to the stock exchanges. Any modification in the URL shall be reported to stock exchanges within 3 days of such changes. Reporting to clients 17. 15.10.1.7, 23.1.1(f) & 48.8 Once the TM settles the running account of funds of a client, an intimation shall be sent to the client by SMS on mobile number and also by email. The intimation should also include details about the transfer of funds (in case of electronic transfer – transaction number and date; in case of physical payment instruments – instrument number and date). TM shall send the retention statement along with the statement of running accounts to the clients as per the existing provisions within five working days.
As on 31st March of every year, a statement of balance of Funds and Securities in hard form and signed by the broker shall be sent to all the clients.

In addition to the e-mail communication of the ECNs in the manner stated above, in order to further strengthen the electronic communication channel, the member shall simultaneously publish the ECN on his designated web- site in a secured way and enable relevant access to the clients.
Contract notes must be issued to clients as per existing regulations, within twenty-four hours of the trade execution.

For information of all investors who deal/ invest/ transact in the market, the offices of all stock brokers (and its authorized person(s)) shall prominently display basic information, as provided in Annexure-36, about the grievance redressal mechanism available to investors.

Stock Brokers shall bring the Investor Charter to the notice of their clients (existing as well as new clients) through disclosing the Investor Charter on their respective websites, making them available at prominent places in the office, provide a copy of Investor Charter as a part of account opening kit to the clients, through e-mails/ letters etc. 234 Technology related reporting requirements 23. 16-Table – 8 (1.5) The system audit report submitted by the auditor should be forwarded to the Stock Exchange by the Stock Broker along with management comments, within one month of submission of report by the auditor.

QSBs shall arrange to have their systems audited on half- yearly basis by a CERT-IN empanelled auditor to check compliance with the above mentioned requirements related to cyber security and other circulars of SEBI on cybersecurity and technical glitches, to the extent they are relevant to them and shall submit the report to stock exchanges along with the comments of the cybersecurity committee within one month of completion of the half year.
A systems audit of the DMA systems and software shall be periodically carried out by the broker as may be specified by the exchange and certificate in this regard shall be submitted to the exchange.

System audit of the Smart Order Routing systems and software shall be periodically carried out by the brokers as may be specified by the exchange and certificate in this regard shall be submitted to the exchange.

The Stock Brokers are mandated to conduct comprehensive cyber audit at least once in a financial year. All Stock Brokers shall submit with Stock Exchange a declaration from the MD/ CEO/ Partners/ Proprietors certifying compliance by the Stock Brokers with all SEBI Circulars and advisories related to Cyber security from time to time, along with the Cyber audit report.

Stock Brokers shall conduct VAPT at least once in a financial year. All Stock Brokers are required to engage only CERT-In empaneled organizations for conducting VAPT. The final report on said VAPT shall be submitted to the Stock Exchanges after approval from Technology Committee of respective Stock Brokers, within 1 month of completion of VAPT activity.

All Cyber-attacks, threats, cyber-incidents and breaches experienced by Stock Brokers shall be reported to Stock Exchanges & SEBI within six hours of noticing / detecting such incidents or being brought to notice about such incidents. This information shall be shared to SEBI through the dedicated e-mail id: sbdp-cyberincidents@sebi.gov.in.

The incident shall also be reported to Indian Computer Emergency Response team (CERT-In) in accordance with 235 the guidelines / directions issued by CERT-In from time to time. Additionally, the Stock Brokers, whose systems have been identified as “Protected system” by National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre (NCIIPC) shall also report the incident to NCIIPC. The quarterly reports containing information on cyber- attacks, threats, cyber-incidents and breaches experienced by Stock Brokers and measures taken to mitigate vulnerabilities, threats and attacks including information on bugs / vulnerabilities, threats that may be useful for other Stock Brokers / Exchanges and SEBI, shall be submitted to Stock Exchanges within 15 days from the quarter ended June, September, December and March of every year (Format for Submitting the reports is attached in below Annexure 25).

The Type I Stock Brokers shall arrange to have their systems audited on an annual basis by a CERT-IN empanelled auditor, an independent DISA (ICAI) Qualification, CISA (Certified Information System Auditor) from ISACA, CISM (Certified Information Securities Manager) from ISACA, CISSP (Certified Information Systems Security Professional) from International Information Systems Security Certification Consortium (commonly known as (ISC)2), to check compliance with the above areas and shall submit the report to Stock Exchanges along with the comments of the Board / Partners / Proprietor of Stock Broker within three months of the end of the financial year.

The compliance of the advisory shall be reported in the half yearly report by stock brokers to stock exchanges with an undertaking, “Compliance of the SEBI circular for Advisory for Financial Sector Organizations regarding Software as a Service (SaaS) based solutions has been made.”
Stock brokers shall inform about the technical glitch to the stock exchanges immediately but not later than one hour from the time of occurrence of the glitch.

Stock brokers shall submit a Preliminary Incident Report to the Exchange within T+1 day of the incident (T being the date of the incident). The report shall include the date and time of the incident, the details of the incident, effect of the incident and the immediate action taken to rectify the problem. 236
Stock brokers shall submit a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) Report (as per Annexure 30) of the technical glitch to stock exchange, within fourteen days from the date of the incident.
Stock brokers shall submit information stated in para 63.3.1, 63.3.2 and 63.3.3 above, by e-mail at infotechglitch@nse.co.in, a common email address for reporting across all stock exchanges.

The compliance of the advisory shall be provided by the REs along with their cybersecurity audit report (conducted as per the applicable SEBI Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience framework). The compliance shall be submitted as per the existing reporting mechanism and frequency of the respective cybersecurity audit. Reporting requirements for QSBs

QSBs shall submit an annual report to the stock exchanges regarding the observations of the committees of BOD or analogous body, corrective action taken by the QSB and measures taken to prevent recurrence of such incidents.

The risk management framework shall have measures for carrying out surveillance of client behaviour through analyzing the pattern of trading done by clients, detection of any unusual activity being done by such clients, reporting the same to stock exchanges.
The risk management policy shall be reviewed on half yearly basis by the QSB and a report in this regard shall be submitted by the risk management committee of the QSB to the stock exchange.

Reporting to Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) - The stock brokers shall be responsible for reporting of any suspicious transactions / reports to FIU or any other competent authority in respect of activities carried out by the third parties. 237
